Indeed this really was the best solution, which was clearly shown on the documentation of what power would be generated by that solution.  So, that is what I had fitted by Solahart.  Over the two years that I have had my panels and battery I have been extremely pleased with their performance, and my electricity bils have been very substantially reduced.  The battery provides with sufficient stored power to outlast a three day loss of power from the grid, which was the main reason I had this work done.  At all times the Solahart workers were extremely efficient and were always so polite in the dealings with me.  I have the upmost confidence in my system and also in Solahart and their workmanship.Barry Fox

Solarhart were excellent to work with!Every aspect of the process was professional from quoting, through install and after sales service.Competitive price, customized solution and above expectation performance of Solar panels, inverter, battery and power outage backup!Highly recommended!

The salesperson actually came to our premises to assess the property and speak to me - definitely better than the others who were based further away from our property. We where very impressed with the salesman and very impressed with the installators, they where very efficient and cleaned the site as they found it, we are very happy.

Solahart provide quality products at a competitive price. The sales and customer service staff were great. The installers were knowledgeable and efficient. Quotation disclosed all relevant details, cost etc.Installation on time and as per discussion on first day of quotation.Removed old 1.4kw system.

Sales process was head and shoulders above the other two quotes, the salesperson punctual, knowledgeable and realistic about the peculiar angles and pitch of the roof and sized the system for best efficiency, rather than the other companies that didnt even visit and just jammed as many panels on any roof face they could using google maps. They also added a hot water timer for no extra cost. I am really impressed with the own-brand 400w silouhette panels they use as well, the research shows them to be higher quality than the competitionInstallation had a long lead time (6 weeks), I assume this is normal in the industry, but when the day did arrive the installation team were excellent, involving me in decision making, panel placement was a team effort and good regard to aesthetics, the team used full roof tethering and scaffold fall protection. They were flexible enough to install another panel when they realised it would fit nicely at a good price. It was a large team of 4 people and the whole thing was done by lunch time. The meter box layout and conduit in the roof were both well laid out and run too.The solaredge system was set up properly with map and layout correctly done, I know not all companies do that. I had a problem with the hot water timer over the weekend and the salesman called me back on his day off and had it sorted the next day sending an electrician out. I think there was some small administrative error in them contacting the wrong company for grid connection/meter configuration, but it was no hassle to fix that up myself.

Interesting, Solahart was not on my initial list of companies but after using Solarquotes it was part of the 3 companies provided to me.I was contacted very promptly by Solahart to arrange a site inspection and consult.  This is the first very important part of the process, a site inspection is a must.  One other company provided me a quote without a site inspection which included a system that would not even physically fit on my roof !The Solahart sales consultant (Rodney) arrived a couple of days later, taking photographs of the property, roof and power circuits.  Rodney was very punctually and well presented.  Rodney provided me with a number of options but without the 'hard sell'.  Before Rodney even left my home, I had a full information package, proposed system, site layout and fixed price quotation. It doesn't get any easier than that people.A few weeks later, the installation team arrived at my home, 3 very well mannered and well presented gentleman.The weather was not the best, rain on and off most of the day but this didn't seem to bother the team who just got on with the job in hand. At the completion of the install you wouldn't even know the guys had been, the site was completely cleaned and all rubbish removed.Yes, I acknowledge its very early days as my system is only a week old, but in regards to Solahart Newcastle I can not speak more highly of them. On Thursday afternoon, December 20, 2018, at 18:30 we had a storm, the ABB inverter worked fine at 19:30, I took a reading but found that the system was dead two hours later at about 22:00 - all indicator lights were dark. Could not restart the inventer no matter what I tried. Checked it again next morning and the system was running fine. I do not like when things repair themselves!  I am assuming that this was an internal system protection feature in action.  Do you agree?We have a 3-phase electricity supply system. Phase 1 powers our household and a part of a 3-phase aircon, phase 2 is used only by the  3-phase aircon, phase 3 powers a pottery studion plus the 3-phase aircon. Our new solar system is wired into the phase 3 because the pottery shed is located next to the meter box. I was under the impression that the inverter somehow  physically re-distributes the generated electricity on all three phases. However, the installer told me that  this is not so. All power not used on our phase 3 is loaded into the grid while phases 1 and 2 always feed directly from the grid. A smart meter, yet to be installed, will  then re-balance the  three phases by accounting methods rather than physically: i.e. kWh's used and generated on all three phases will be added up into a single number, multiplied by either our retail electricity rate ($0.30) or by the feed-in tarif ($0.10) and then charged against our electricity account.  If this is so all will be fine.  Your articlehttps://support.solarquotes.com.au/hc/en-us/articles/115001596554-How-does-a-single-phase-inverter-on-a-3-phase-supply-affect-my-self-consumption-confirms this explanation.  Otherewise we would have a serious wiring problem.I would also like to use this opportunty to thank  you for all the valuable information that your website provides. It is one of the few steady light spots in this current wild solar installers jungle!Best regards,Jorge Tlaskal
